name: Dioctyltin diacetate
description: Dioctyltin diacetate (CAS 17586-94-6 ), also known as Bis(n-octyl)tin diacetate, is an organotin compound used industrially as a catalyst and curing agent across polymer and coating systems. It accelerates condensation reactions and crosslinking processes, enabling controlled cure rates in demanding manufacturing environments. In silicone sealants and elastomers, it functions as a room-temperature vulcanization catalyst. This material drives crosslink formation in one- and two-component systems used in construction and industrial assembly. PVC stabilization compounding relies on organotin chemistry to manage thermal degradation during processing. Dioctyltin compounds offer compatibility with flexible formulations in these applications. Polyurethane and adhesive formulators use it to initiate and regulate polymerization, controlling open time and final bond strength. In structural applications, coatings manufacturers incorporate it into moisture-cure systems. Precise catalytic activity determines film formation speed and surface quality in these specialized industrial coatings. Dioctyltin diacetate is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial concentrations, suitable for direct incorporation into formulation processes. This ensures ease of use during large scale chemical manufacturing. Technical grade is the primary market offering, with specifications typically aligned to organotin catalyst standards for industrial use. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers for production. These delivery formats reflect its use in continuous production environments.
